title: Operator Console: Throttle & Provisioning Logbook
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an operator-facing logbook and fast controls in the Console that let SREs and capacity operators understand, override, and replay fleet-level scaling decisions. The feature ties together throughput guarantees, autoscaling policies, and an immutable change history so teams can diagnose incidents and meet customer SLAs.

Scope: UI surfaces + lightweight API plumbing. Not in scope: deep runtime change handlers (ENG will deliver hooks). Deliverables: 1) 'Pace Controls' quick-adjust panel for on-call overrides, 2) Provisioning Logbook (chronological, filterable, diff view), 3) Throughput Pulse dashboard widget (per-fleet throughput vs guaranteed SLO), 4) Policy edit link that surfaces active autoscaling policy and suggested fallback.

Design principles: make operator actions reversible where safe, expose exact token throughput numbers and the underlying capacity tokens used, and ensure the audit trail is immutable and exportable. Provide guardrails for manual overrides (requires reason, TTL, and RBAC check).

Acceptance criteria:
- Pace Controls panel allows manual throttle/provision adjustments with min/max guards, TTL, and required reason field.
- Provisioning Logbook shows immutable entries with timestamp, actor, change type (policy-edit, manual-override, automatic-scale, rollback), and before/after capacity and throughput.
- Logbook supports filters (fleet, actor, change-type, time-range), a side-by-side diff for capacity/throughput deltas, and CSV export.
- Throughput Pulse widget shows 1m/1h/24h histograms, current SLO vs actual throughput, and links to related rollout/incident.
- All operator actions create audit entries and surface links to GitHub PRs or Confluence runbooks when present.
- Unit tests and E2E smoke test for policy edits and manual overrides are added.

Open questions:
- TTL default for manual overrides: 30m or 1h? (ops preference leaning to 1h)
- Should throttles be applied at route-level by default or fleet-level? (start fleet-level, route-level as follow-up)
- CSV export scope: all fields or paginated exports? (start with full export of filtered view)

Related artifacts:
